author: WPB6
summary: Alpha.1-era (2026-08-11) read-only audit of sharp-runtime, easy-gl, meta-gl, free-direct and free-api against CNA 7a64362e. The sharp-runtime and sibling deep dives already carry nearly all of it at newer sibling revisions (sharp-runtime next 41b918c9, easy-gl deda7a42, meta-gl 20c8b2dc), with several audit claims corrected (header counts, component selection under CNA, DesktopEsTier as the sharing mechanism). Residue added: what else free-api's headers bring into the FREEDIRECT translation units beyond the fopen macro (include directories, byte and Win32 name macros, case shims, unsupported areas).

concepts.text: sharp-runtime is a C++23 reimplementation of a practical subset of the .NET base class library that reproduces the System:: namespace tree literally rather than inventing a vanity namespace.

target.evidence: sharp-runtime 41b918c9 README; already stated on the components page

concepts.text: Modules are registered through a custom CMake registry (sharp_runtime_register_module / sharp_runtime_register_component) with globbed sources; directory count, registered names and dependency edges are different measures.
concepts.note: Audit: 41 directories, 44 components (30 STATIC, 13 INTERFACE, 1 ALIAS). At 41b918c9: 44 directories, 47 registered names (33 STATIC, 13 INTERFACE, 1 alias); Xml.XPath is still the alias of Xml.

concepts.text: There is no umbrella header: every public header sits under System/ or SharpRuntime/, and the path is a mechanical transliteration of the .NET fully qualified type name, one type per header.
System::String is not a string class: its constructor and destructor are deleted, it offers static helpers over std::string, and the value type is std::string, also exported as SharpRuntime::String.
System::Object is not a universal root: it is abstract (pure virtual GetTypeName()) and only a handful of library classes derive from it, so sharp-runtime has no rooted object model.
concepts.note: Audit: exactly two derived classes; at 41b918c9 three (DateTime, DateTimeOffset, System::Timers::Timer). CNA's own XNA layer derives many classes from Object.

concepts.text: System::Exception derives from std::exception, carries an inner exception as std::exception_ptr and an HResult defaulting to 0x80131500, returns an empty StackTrace, and deliberately omits GetBaseException() and ToString(); there is no ThrowHelper.

target.evidence: sharp-runtime Exception.hpp; object-model page (about 114 exception classes at 41b918c9; audit ~111)

concepts.text: Type::From<T>() is genuine RTTI-backed type identity, usable as a service key, but Type's predicates return fixed values that are not mutually consistent; Activator is template-only.
Lifetime is value semantics plus RAII: std::shared_ptr only where .NET reference identity matters, no custom smart pointer, and System::GC methods are no-ops.

Type families by area: strings and encodings, generic/immutable/concurrent/frozen collections with a fail-fast mutation counter, streams whose capability properties are virtual with defaults, filesystem facades, and a full threading and task surface.
tokens: lightweight subset of the .NET Stream API

concepts.text: SharpRuntimeHelper.hpp is the primitive-alias header (intcs, charcs as char16_t, PascalCase aliases, the native int128 macro) and also defines the unnamespaced macros CONTAINS and INTERNAL, a collision hazard for every includer.
concepts.note: Included by 389 public headers at 41b918c9 (audit: 367).

concepts.text: Prop.hpp is a pure macro header of declare/implement property generators (DDATA/IDATA, DGETTER/IGETTER, DGETTERSTATIC) built on token pasting; its main consumer is CNA, not sharp-runtime.
concepts.note: Audit: zero sharp-runtime modules include it. At 41b918c9 two Experimental property headers do; CNA's public headers use it, so its 31 macro names reach game code (issue candidate recorded by WP16).

concepts.text: CNA consumes sharp-runtime through System/ include paths that mirror .NET names; counting only the SharpRuntime/ prefix mistakes a namespace prefix for a repository boundary.

Parity strategy: maximum practical parity with .NET; an unimplementable method throws NotImplementedException with a comment, a platform gap throws PlatformNotSupportedException, and a silent wrong value is never acceptable.

Permanent deviations: reflection stubs as end state, GC no-ops, three delegate tiers with DynamicInvoke always throwing, serialization ignored, P/Invoke out of scope, and symmetric/asymmetric crypto and TLS out of scope by a dated 2026-07-07 decision.

target.evidence: sharp-runtime CLAUDE.md known permanent deviations at 41b918c9

concepts.note: At 41b918c9 the list is longer and serialization narrowed (SerializationInfo is a real store since 2026-09-20); the site gives the current list.

concepts.text: Naming: PascalCase with getXxxProperty()/setXxxProperty() accessors and getItem()/setItem() indexers; no LINQ in project code; the rules forbid a broad header refactor because naming touches 449+ files and would break CNA.

Parity work is anchored to a .NET reference-source checkout at an absolute path outside the repository, neither vendored nor pinned, so the parity process is not reproducible from the repository alone.

sharp-runtime keeps tests in three places: modules/<m>/tests (primary GoogleTest), tests/ (cross-component integration and an i686 boundary source) and test/ (Python meta-tests and consumer fixtures, some of which must fail to compile).

Each component gets its own test executable linked only to that component and its declared test dependencies, so a test reaching across an undeclared module edge fails to link; an empty dependency allowlist and a source-partition validator back this up.
Test scale at the audit: 16,310 tests in 37 executables with 6 failing; five modules without tests, among them a regular-expression module with no implementation.
concepts.note: At 41b918c9 the README baseline is 17,840 tests in 38 executables (2026-08-22), four module directories own no tests, and Regex is implemented inline over std::regex; dated counts are not pass claims.

CNA adds the sibling from CNA_SHARP_RUNTIME_ROOT (default ../sharp-runtime) with add_subdirectory; it is not a submodule, there is no vendored copy or FetchContent fallback, and a missing checkout stops the configure with a clone command.

concepts.text: easy-gl was audited on develop @ 0b46d35c (2026-08-07, 85 commits); CNA 009d40f5 needs easy-gl deda7a42 or later because it sets EASYGL_EMSCRIPTEN_EXCEPTION_MODEL.
easy-gl is a toolkit-independent RAII/OOP C++ wrapper over OpenGL and OpenGL ES, built on meta-gl; the host owns window, context, events and presentation and supplies a GetProcAddress callback.

target.evidence: easy-gl README at deda7a42; easy-gl/meta-gl deep dive

concepts.text: easy-gl adds ../meta-gl as a sibling subdirectory and links it publicly; CNA's configure error names that second sibling requirement.

easy-gl's public API is namespace easygl with resource classes (Buffer, Program, Texture, VertexArray and more), support types (Device, Capabilities) and RAII helpers (ScopedBind, ScopedDebugGroup, ResourceRegistry, UniformCache).
easy-gl resource classes are move-only RAII owners over meta-gl's typed handles, with a generation-tracked base that supports context-loss detection.
easy-gl reports missing features with C++ exceptions (UnsupportedFeatureException) while meta-gl terminates, which forces one exception ABI across the WebAssembly build.

target.evidence: easy-gl cmake/EasyGlPlatform.cmake at deda7a42; CNA sets EASYGL_EMSCRIPTEN_EXCEPTION_MODEL=JS

concepts.note: Audit: -fwasm-exceptions applied globally; since deda7a42 the exception ABI is selectable and CNA selects JS.

concepts.text: easy-gl's WebGL support reuses meta-gl's context detection, guards optional entry points with IsFunctionAvailable() and throws instead of calling null pointers, requires GL_OES_vertex_array_object below ES 3.0, and records separable pipelines as permanently absent on WebGL.
easy-gl's four hand-rolled test executables use fake loaders and need no GPU; the two desktop-shaped suites are not built under Emscripten.

easy-gl defaults EASYGL_BUILD_TESTS and EASYGL_BUILD_EXAMPLES to ON and CNA does not force them off for native GL builds, so a CNA GL build compiles easy-gl's tests, unlike sharp-runtime's which CNA disables.

concepts.note: At 009d40f5 CNA's web preset sets both OFF; every other configuration inherits the ON defaults (issue candidates WP17-i003/i004).

concepts.text: free-direct develop @ 934f72ff (2026-07-18) with no later commit on any ref.
free-direct is a C++20 reimplementation of a narrow, game-driven subset of DirectX 3 (2D only) over SDL3, layered on free-api, scoped by two target games.
free-direct implements DirectDraw, DirectSound and DirectPlay interfaces; Direct3D is absent, and all three public headers include free-api's windows.h.
Every public free-direct method carries a Doxygen status tag; the 95 tags split 56 IMPLEMENTED, 23 PARTIAL and 16 STUB, reproducible with a grep.

free-direct's internal namespaces are snake_case (free_direct_directdraw and others) while its public headers are global-namespace, DirectX-shaped C++; one source reaches into free-api's platform namespace.
concepts.note: Internal namespaces are implementation detail CNA never sees; the page states the public shape.

concepts.text: free-direct's DirectDraw is real (CPU pixel buffers uploaded on Flip, Blt/BltFast, Lock/Unlock) and its two documented stubs, IsLost() and Restore(), always succeed.
free-direct's DirectSound (SDL3 audio streams, centibel volume, constant-power pan, a 64 MiB buffer ceiling) and inline DirectPlay implementation, including two near-empty translation units.
tokens: DirectSound and DirectPlay stay out by design
concepts.note: CNA uses only DirectDraw; the page scopes free-direct to what CNA consumes and summarises the other two parts.

concepts.text: free-direct's ENet transport is opt-in (FREE_DIRECT_ENABLE_ENET, default OFF), so a stock build has only in-process loopback DirectPlay.
free-direct machine-enforces header hygiene: a script fails if any SDL3, SDL3_net or ENet identifier appears in include/.
free-direct's hand-rolled tests are off by default, and its DirectPlay suite deliberately fails loopback-oriented checks when ENet is enabled.
free-direct has three consumers: the two games add ../free-api explicitly before ../free-direct, while CNA relies on free-direct pulling free-api in itself.

CNA's FREEDIRECT renderer is a deep consumer: a CPU SpriteBatch compositor through locked surfaces, a shadow back buffer, a resize transaction with failure injection, and tests that read back through the shadow buffer under the dummy video driver.
concepts.note: Audit: 8 registered CTests; at 009d40f5 the family's examples CMake registers 21.

concepts.text: free-api's windows.h globally defines fopen as free_api_fopen; CNA contains it by keeping <ddraw.h> out of FreeDirectRenderer.hpp and behind a pimpl in one translation unit.

Beyond fopen, <ddraw.h> brings free-api's compat include directories (include/ and include_non_windows/) into both FreeDirect translation units through PUBLIC links, and macros such as byte, the A-suffix Win32 names (MessageBox), RGB, TRUE/FALSE and MAX_PATH, but no min/max.

concepts.text: free-api develop @ 53d7a312 (2026-07-18) with no later commit on any ref.
free-api is a static C++20 library reimplementing a deliberately tiny ~1998-era Win32 subset over SDL3 for two games; it is explicitly not Wine.
tokens: neither Wine nor a general Win32 SDK

concepts.text: CNA depends on free-api transitively and non-optionally whenever FREEDIRECT is selected, through free-direct's PUBLIC link; CNA's own CMake names free-api only in comments.
free-api's public surface is C: about eighty extern "C" WINAPI declarations across 23 flat Win32-named headers with windows.h as umbrella, each carrying a status tag.
free-api's include_non_windows/ directory is a case-sensitivity shim (Windows.h, WinUser.h forwarders) plus a real sys/timeb.h, exported through the freeapi_compat_headers INTERFACE target.
free_api_bridge.h is the deliberate seam for free-direct: three functions (FreeApiCreateSurfaceDC, FreeApiDestroySurfaceDC, FreeApiSetWindowFullscreen).

free-api's subsystems are real (message queue, windows over SDL_Window, input, GDI-lite, file shims, timers, MCI/MIDI, joystick, string resources); HWND is an SDL_Window* cast to void* and no SDL type is public.
free-api depends only on SDL3, SDL3_image and SDL3_mixer plus vendored TinySoundFont/TinyMidiLoader; version floors apply only when it finds a system SDL itself.
concepts.note: The floors (3.4.0/3.4.0/3.2.0) apply under FREE_API_USE_SYSTEM_SDL3, not to CNA's vendored SDL targets.

The book's ecosystem account of free-api was substantively right apart from two renamed identifiers, and its free-api line count still reproduces.
